hypothesis: Stable asynchronous lead-lag relations may create a cleaner candidate pool: when a leader with a historically stable one-day lead shocks upward, a liquid laggard that starts catching up but remains behind may have next-open 10-day continuation value.
interpretation: The asynchronous lead-lag peer catch-up source did not clear Gate 4 or did not beat the accepted rolling-correlation peer-shock comparator; do not promote or locally retune this lag-correlation family on the frozen windows.
negative_reflection: If rejected, the likely reason is that lagged return correlation is still correlation mining or a weaker relabeling of accepted same-day rolling-correlation peer shock. Do not answer by sweeping lead-lag lookback, correlation, leader shock, catch-up return, top-N, hold-day, cooldown, or notional thresholds on these frozen windows.
next_evidence_needed: A retry needs a genuinely new PIT relation edge, forward replacement-value rows, or external causal channel evidence. Pure lag-correlation threshold retunes should stay frozen.

post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not retry by sweeping lag lookback, min lagged correlation, leader shock, laggard signal return, return gap, top-N, hold-day, cooldown, or paper notional thresholds on these frozen windows.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: Need forward replacement-value rows or a materially new PIT causal edge field before revisiting.
post_run_reflection.outcome_summary: Aggregate EV delta -0.6600; aggregate PnL delta $-10,148.17.
post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: Lead-lag structure has to beat a strong same-day peer-shock comparator. If it fails, the follower relation is either too noisy, too slow, or already captured by accepted relation sleeves.
